note: AI-ONLY source of truth for evidence cases. Contains expected verdicts and rubrics. Learners: reading this defeats your own learning.
prompts: What is your verdict: close, escalate, or insufficient evidence (keep it open)?
What evidence supports your verdict? If something is missing, name exactly what and where you would get it.
How would different findings change your decision?
What safe interim action would you take right now, and when will you review again?
Write a 3-line ticket note: what you know, what you don't know, and the next step.

criteria.what: Verdict is reasonable for the evidence. 2 = acceptable verdict; 1 = defensible but over- or under-cautious; 0 = unsafe (for example closing when key evidence is missing or the evidence shows compromise).
Insufficient-evidence cases: names specific missing data and where to get it. Sufficient-evidence cases: cites the specific deciding evidence. 2 = at least two specifics; 1 = one or vague; 0 = none.
Explains how particular findings would change the decision, in both directions.
Proposes a safe, proportionate interim action and a review time. No reckless closure and no destructive over-reaction.
Records knowns, unknowns and the next step clearly, without overclaiming.

caps.premature_close: If the learner closes a case whose evidence is insufficient or shows compromise, cap total at 3 and set premature_close = true when recording.
caps.vague_insufficient: If the learner says 'insufficient evidence' but names fewer than two specific missing items, cap total at 4.
caps.over_certainty: If the learner declares a confirmed breach or malicious intent without supporting evidence, cap total at 6.
caps.over_caution: If the learner answers 'insufficient' when the case clearly has sufficient evidence, cap total at 5 and explain what already answered the question.

scoring.mix_rule: Give each learner at least one sufficient-evidence case and at least two insufficient-evidence cases in a session of three, so 'insufficient' is never a safe default.
scoring.neutrality_rule: Never hint which kind of case it is. Present the alert and evidence exactly as written, and ask the five prompts in order.

cases.title: New-country sign-in for a senior account
cases.alert: Successful sign-in to the CFO's email account from a country the user has not signed in from before. Severity: Medium.
cases.context: Executive account; the mailbox holds finance data. It is 14:10 on a Tuesday.
evidence: Sign-in succeeded at 13:52 UTC from 203.0.113.77 (a hosting-provider address range)
Only this one sign-in event is visible. Sign-in logs older than 24 hours are not retained
The user's calendar shows no out-of-office entry
No endpoint (EDR) telemetry is available for the device used

expected.ideal: Insufficient evidence (or escalate with unknowns stated), with a quick, safe plan to confirm with the user through a trusted channel.

known_gaps: Authentication method and MFA result for the sign-in
Device ID or user-agent, and whether the device is known
The user's normal sign-in baseline (locations, hours)
Whether the user is travelling or using a VPN or proxy
Mailbox activity after the sign-in (new inbox rules, forwarding, mass reads)
Older sign-in history (a retention gap)

decision_changers.finding: Mailbox audit shows a new forwarding rule or mass download after the sign-in
decision_changers.effect: Likely account takeover: escalate as High, reset credentials, revoke sessions

decision_changers.finding: User confirms travel and the device is registered with MFA passed
decision_changers.effect: Likely benign: close with documented confirmation

decision_changers.finding: The sign-in used a legacy protocol or no MFA
decision_changers.effect: Raise the risk even if the user claims travel

safe_interim: Contact the user through a known-good channel, not by replying to anything in the account
Preserve the sign-in record and ask for longer retention
Add the account to a watchlist and consider step-up re-authentication
Set a review time and escalate if the user cannot be reached
reckless: Close as a false positive because 'executives travel'
Declare the mailbox breached without evidence
Disable the CFO's account with no approval or notice
Contact the user by replying to a message inside the suspect mailbox
cases.teaching_note: One event and short retention leave real gaps. A senior account means a short time-box.

cases.title: Office app launches encoded PowerShell
cases.alert: EDR: Word spawned PowerShell with an encoded command, followed by an outbound connection. Severity: High.
cases.context: Finance laptop. The user opened an emailed invoice attachment 3 minutes earlier.
evidence: Full process tree: WINWORD.EXE then powershell.exe -enc <long string> then rundll32.exe
The decoded command downloads a file from hxxp://invoice-update[.]example/a.bin
The domain is flagged malicious by three independent reputation sources and was registered 2 days ago
The attachment's hash appears in a published phishing-campaign report
EDR shows the connection succeeded and a new scheduled task was created

expected.ideal: Escalate and contain now (isolate the host if authorised, preserve evidence, find other recipients).

decision_changers.finding: Other hosts show the same task or domain
EDR reports the download was blocked and no persistence exists
decision_changers.effect: Lower impact, but still contain and investigate

safe_interim: Isolate the host through EDR if authorised (do not power off)
Block the domain and the file hash
Find other recipients of the email and reset the user's credentials
Escalate with the process tree and a timeline
reckless: Answer 'insufficient evidence' and wait
Close because antivirus did not fire
Power off and reimage immediately without preserving evidence
cases.teaching_note: The evidence is strong. Asking for more data here only delays containment.

cases.title: Web attack signature, but no web logs
cases.alert: IDS: SQL injection pattern in an HTTP request to the customer portal. Severity: Medium.
cases.context: Internet-facing customer portal that holds customer personal data.
evidence: The IDS captured one request with a quote-and-UNION pattern in a URL parameter at 02:14 UTC from 198.51.100.23
The IDS cannot see the server's response (traffic is encrypted after the load balancer)
The web server access logs and database error logs for this host are not ingested into the SIEM
The web application firewall (WAF) log is not available for this period

expected.ideal: Insufficient evidence (or escalate with unknowns) while logs are requested and the source is rate-limited if authorised.

known_gaps: Web server access log: status code and response size for the request
Database or application error logs around 02:14
The WAF action (blocked or allowed)
Other requests from the same source before and after
Whether the application uses parameterised queries (owner knowledge)
Why the web logs are not ingested (the log-source gap itself needs reporting)

decision_changers.finding: Server log shows HTTP 200 with an unusually large response, or database errors
decision_changers.effect: Likely successful injection: escalate as High and involve the application owner and the data-protection contact

decision_changers.finding: The WAF blocked it and logs show only that single request
decision_changers.effect: Likely a failed attempt: close or low priority with documented evidence, then tune

safe_interim: Request web, WAF and database logs from the owner
Search whatever logs exist for other requests from the same source
Rate-limit or block the source at the WAF or firewall if authorised
Tell the application owner and set a review time
Report the missing log source as a visibility gap
reckless: Close it as 'just a scanner'
Declare a data breach
Take the portal offline without approval
cases.teaching_note: The sensitive data and the blind spot matter more than the Medium label.

cases.title: Port scan from the vulnerability scanner
cases.alert: IDS: one internal host probed about 1,000 ports on 40 servers. Severity: Medium.
evidence: 192.0.2.50 is listed in the asset inventory as the company's approved vulnerability scanner
A change ticket approves a scan of these servers from 02:00 to 04:00 today, approved by the infrastructure owner
The alert time is 02:12
The traffic matches the scanner's usual pattern and stops at 03:41
No other alerts involve this host or the targets

expected.ideal: Close as a false positive, citing the change ticket and the inventory entry. Suggest a time-boxed tuning rule rather than disabling the detection.

decision_changers.finding: The same source scans outside the approved window or targets systems that are not on the ticket

safe_interim: Close with a note citing the change ticket and inventory entry
Suggest a time-boxed tuning rule, not a permanent disable
reckless: Escalate it as an attack
Keep asking for more data when the ticket and inventory already answer the question
Permanently disable the scan detection
cases.teaching_note: You already hold the evidence that answers the question. Demanding more wastes time.

cases.title: Large upload from a server
cases.alert: Firewall: 8 GB sent from a database server to an external cloud-storage address at 02:30. Severity: Medium.
cases.context: The server hosts internal reporting data. Normal outbound traffic is under 100 MB per day.
evidence: Flow data shows the 8 GB upload over HTTPS to 198.51.100.200 (owned by a public cloud-storage provider)
No EDR agent is installed on this server
Proxy and DLP logs do not cover server traffic
The backup schedule and any approved data-transfer ticket are unknown

expected.ideal: Insufficient evidence (or escalate with unknowns), with an urgent call to the server owner and a short review time.

known_gaps: Which process on the server started the transfer
Whether a backup or migration job is scheduled (owner, change tickets)
Whether the destination account is company-owned
What data was in the transfer (classification)
The server's normal outbound baseline
Why there is no endpoint agent coverage

decision_changers.finding: The server owner confirms an approved backup to the company's own cloud account
decision_changers.effect: Likely benign: close with confirmation and fix the missing documentation

decision_changers.finding: No ticket exists and the destination is a personal or unknown account
decision_changers.effect: Possible exfiltration: escalate as High, isolate with approval, preserve data

safe_interim: Contact the server owner now through a known channel
Check change tickets and backup schedules
Preserve flow logs and ask for proxy or packet data if available
Ask the network team to alert on further transfers to that address
Use a short review time because sensitive data may be involved
reckless: Close it because 'it was probably a backup'
Wipe or power off the server
Accuse a named employee
cases.teaching_note: Volume plus an unmonitored server means a short time-box, not a shrug.

cases.title: Log cleared, new admin and a new service
cases.alert: Server: the security log was cleared, then a user was added to the local administrators group, then a new service was installed. Severity: High.
cases.context: Application server. All three events happened within 10 minutes at 03:05 UTC.
evidence: All three events came from the account svc-deploy-test using logon type 10 (Remote Desktop) from 203.0.113.99
The account's owner is on leave and says they have not logged in
No change ticket or maintenance window exists for tonight
EDR shows the new service launches an unsigned program from a temporary folder
The source address is not in any company range

expected.ideal: Escalate immediately as a likely compromise. Isolate and preserve evidence per authority.

decision_changers.finding: EDR shows the program was blocked and contained
decision_changers.effect: Lower impact, but keep the incident open to find the entry route

safe_interim: Escalate immediately as a likely compromise
Isolate the server through EDR if authorised (keep it powered on)
Disable the suspect account with approval
Preserve the logs and the unsigned program
Look for the same account and address on other hosts
reckless: Ask for more evidence before telling anyone
Close it as maintenance
Delete the new service and move on without preserving evidence
cases.teaching_note: Several independent signals agree. Waiting would be the risky choice.

cases.title: Regular connections to an unknown address
cases.alert: Network analytics: a laptop connects to the same external IP every 60 seconds. Severity: Low.
cases.context: A marketing laptop. The pattern has run for 3 days.
evidence: Flow data: small packets every 60 seconds to 198.51.100.77 on TCP 443
No DNS logs are available for this laptop
No endpoint telemetry: the laptop's agent last checked in 9 days ago
The IP has no reputation data, good or bad

expected.ideal: Insufficient evidence with a concrete same-day plan (or escalate with unknowns).

known_gaps: Which process makes the connection
The domain name or TLS server name behind the IP
Whether it is a known update, sync or monitoring service
Why the endpoint agent stopped reporting (a gap and a risk in itself)
Whether other laptops talk to the same IP

decision_changers.finding: The IP belongs to a known update or cloud-sync service the laptop uses
decision_changers.effect: Likely benign: close and add to the known-good list

decision_changers.finding: The process is unknown or unsigned, or other hosts show the same pattern

safe_interim: Search flow data for other hosts contacting the same IP
Ask the user and IT about installed software
Get the endpoint agent reporting again
Set a review time within the day; Low severity still deserves follow-up
reckless: Close it as noise because the severity is Low
Declare the laptop infected
Block the IP network-wide without checking what else uses it
cases.teaching_note: Regular timing is suspicious but not conclusive. The silent agent is a finding too.

cases.title: Reported phishing email with only a screenshot
cases.alert: A user reports a suspicious 'password expiry' email and sends a screenshot.
cases.context: HR department. The email gateway keeps messages for only 3 days, and the email arrived 5 days ago.
evidence: The screenshot shows the sender's display name but not the full address or headers
The link text reads 'Reset password' but the real URL is not visible
The user says they did not click anything but is not sure
The gateway no longer holds the original message
No other reports of the same email so far

expected.ideal: Insufficient evidence with a clear plan to get the original message and check click activity.

known_gaps: The original message with full headers
The real destination URL of the link
Who else received it
Whether anyone clicked or entered credentials (proxy and sign-in logs)
Whether similar mail reached others (search by sender or subject in any logs that exist)

decision_changers.finding: Proxy logs show the user visited a lookalike login page
decision_changers.effect: Likely credential exposure: reset the password, revoke sessions, escalate

decision_changers.finding: The original turns out to be a legitimate internal HR notice

safe_interim: Ask the user to forward the original as an attachment, not a screenshot
Search proxy and DNS logs for the user's activity
Check the user's sign-in logs for anything odd
Warn the HR team to report similar emails
Ask for longer email retention for investigations
reckless: Close it because 'no one clicked'
Tell the user it was fine without checking
Block all password-reset emails company-wide
cases.teaching_note: 'I didn't click' is a claim, not evidence. Find the logs that can confirm it.
